Subject: June 24 webinar — lead export and KPI summary

Jordan,

Attached is the raw lead export and our KPI summary from the June 24 "State of Retrieval" webinar. Quick highlights:~70% of registrants opened the product trial link, 42% clicked the sponsor session (Redwood Inference), and 18 net opportunities were tagged by our team as sales-qualified within two weeks.

I've attached: SP-LeadExport-20260624.csv (lead-level rows with utm tags), June24-Webinar-KPIs.pdf (summary deck), and a short notes spreadsheet with session timestamps.

A couple of things we noted that may affect your pipeline attribution:
- Our form captured both "company_size" and "role" fields; several enterprise leads had company_name blank and came through as "company: -" which your CRM maps to "unknown".
- Some copy on the registration page had an extra utm_source parameter for our internal ad partner, which may have overridden the campaign UTM for orgs that came through the partner funnel.

If you want, Alex and I can walk through a filtered export tomorrow and flag anything obvious for manual re-tagging.

Thanks,
Ellen Evans
Partnerships Lead, DataSummit Media
SwitchPoint Events

Attachments: SP-LeadExport-20260624.csv (text/csv), June24-Webinar-KPIs.pdf (application/pdf)

Team — forwarding the export from DataSummit / SwitchPoint. The external deck claims 18 SQs; our pipeline shows 11 influenced opps and a separate set of 9 unassigned contacts. There are three immediate asks: 

1) Ben — can you triage the 18 SQs Ellen mentions and confirm which are already in HubSpot as Contacts/Deals and which need new records? Please add the HubSpot link(s) or deal IDs in a reply.

2) Marissa — the export shows inconsistent utm_campaign fields and a stray utm_source value that might be the partner override. Can you work with SwitchPoint (Ellen/Alex cc'd) to line up which param took precedence for a sample of 200 leads? We want to determine whether to credit marketing or channel.

3) Lauren — operational ask: for future registrations we should require company_name for enterprise tiers and add a hidden referral_code param so partner-referred leads don't clobber utm_campaign. Could you prep a one-page change request for the platform by EOW?

Plan: we'll reconcile the lead file today; if we can't reach agreement on 6 deals we escalate to contracts for crediting.

Thanks — Jordan
Head of Partnerships (acting), Redwood Inference

Thanks for looping me in. Quick retro notes and proposed fix list based on the export and the session recordings: 

- Root cause: partner ad tag (utm_source=sp_affiliate) was injected by a redirect rule in the registration flow for partner traffic. That override happened for ~14% of registrants and explains the mismatch between SwitchPoint's "sponsor session" clicks and our campaign tally.

- Short fixes (implement within two weeks):
  * Make company_name required for Enterprise registration (form change).
  * Add hidden field referral_code to preserve partner attribution (switchpoint_ref).
  * Update our ingestion script to prefer referral_code over utm_source when present, and to write a normalized lead_source enum.

- Tactical reconciliation guidance:
  * For the six net-new contacts Ben found, mark them as "Channel (SwitchPoint)" if referral_code exists or if SwitchPoint confirms they manually routed those leads. Otherwise mark as "Marketing - Webinar".
  * For the 11 deals already in HubSpot, add a note with session timestamp and set first_touch property if not present.

- Follow-up: I'll schedule 30 minutes with Ellen/Alex for Monday to confirm the redirect rule and get them to export the partner flow sample CSV (they suggested a filtered 500-row sample). Jordan — if you approve, I'll send calendar invites.

Marissa Cole
Field Marketing Lead, Redwood Inference

Attachment: postevent-retro-notes-v1.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)
